newsitem.title: UK: DMG suspends pension fund head Nicola Horlick.
newsitem.headline: DMG suspends pension fund head Nicola Horlick.

text.p: Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, the investment banking arm of Germany's Deutsche Bank, confirmed on Tuesday it had suspended Nicola Horlick, head of Morgan Grenfell Asset Management's pension fund business.

"We have suspended her today pending the outcome of an internal investigation which will look at a potential breach of her contract. It has nothing to do with the Peter Young affair nor any suggestion of financial impropriety," DMG spokesman James Murray told Reuters.

Last year, MGAM fund manager Young was sacked on grounds of gross misconduct following the suspension of trading in three funds, after irregularities were discovered in valuations. Young, who said he was not guilty of any criminal activity, is being investigated by Britain's Serious Fraud Office.

The affair has already led to high-level casualties at MGAM, with a purge in October of senior management, including chief executive Keith Percy and three other directors, after an internal probe revealed "management failings".

And in December, Deutsche Bank agreed to a record compensation package of around 200 million pounds ($334.5 million) to make good losses to investors who lost out as a result of the affair. MGAM is still under investigation by investments watchdog IMRO, which is expected to impose a record fine on the firm.

Murray said DMG would complete its probe into the potential breach of contract by Horlick "as quickly as possible" but said her suspension was "purely internal" and had no regulatory dimension or link to last year's events.
